prompt: I'm looking at A/B test data and the new feature looks like it has a positive effect overall (+2.1% conversion). But when I split by user segment (mobile vs desktop), the effect is NEGATIVE in both segments. How is this possible and which result should I trust?
assertions: Claude identifies this as Simpson's paradox (or describes the equivalent phenomenon by name or mechanism)
Claude explains that the resolution depends on the causal structure — specifically on whether segment is a confounder or a mediator relative to the treatment-conversion relationship
Claude distinguishes the confounder case (segment imbalanced across arms → use disaggregated results) from the mediator case (treatment changes device behavior → use aggregated results)
Claude does NOT just recommend trusting one view (aggregate or segment-level) without considering the DAG — and gives the user a concrete diagnostic to determine which case they're in
